executive_assessment.text: Kara/Savanes planting stress and Greater Lomé/Maritime/Plateaux flooding give dated subnational climate evidence; Savanes food-security concentration is not a local prevalence rate.
Named prefecture access restrictions and displacement-related service gaps deepen FCV context, while national warning and child-policy material describes capacity and remaining gaps.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-08-28 reports: FAO reports that early-season dryness and erratic rain delayed planting and required replanting in parts of Kara and Savanes; early-August satellite data showed below-average vegetation pockets in northern Kara.

FAO's August 2026 brief places about 45% of the nationally estimated June–August CH Phase 3 population in Savanes. It separately reports insecurity-related livelihood/trade disruption and about 13,400 IDPs as of June.
Source dated 2026-08-28 reports: FAO reports late-June 2026 heavy rain flooded Greater Lomé and parts of Maritime and Plateaux, affecting about 26,600 people and damaging housing and infrastructure.

Source dated 2025-04-14 reports: UNICEF reports 16 IED explosions in 2024 limited emergency actors’ access in Kpendjal, Kpendjal Ouest, Tône and Tandjoaré; 31 armed-group attacks or incursions caused 49 deaths and displacement.

Source dated 2025-04-14 reports: UNICEF reports a bad 2024 rainy season flooded Maritime and Grand Lomé, affecting 42,000 people; its regional overview says floods damaged crops and infrastructure and displaced communities.

Source dated 2025-04-14 reports: By October 2024, UNICEF recorded 49,607 displaced people nationally, including 39,436 refugees and 10,171 IDPs; it reports displaced people in 71 Savanes localities had limited access to water, sanitation, health care, education and protection services.

known_gaps.text: The 2025 World Bank CCDR and 2026 government NDC were not substantively accessible; claims rely on opened 2021 and 2023 government reports.
The ministry describes climate-related conflict risks qualitatively; no event-level causal assessment or current local conflict dataset was inspected.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
Reported drought/conflict co-occurrence is not causal event analysis.

No inspected new source establishes that climate hazards caused armed-group violence, farmer-herder conflict or other violence in Togo; the new evidence reports insecurity-related food and access effects without inferring climate causation.
The UNICEF 2024 report's attacks and access restrictions refer to 2024; they are not evidence of current access conditions in October 2026.
FAO's 28 August 2026 crop brief is a dated snapshot; seasonal projections were not presented as verified harvest outcomes.
WMO lists the hydromet project as completed but does not document delivered outputs or warning effectiveness on the accessible page.
The full French UNICEF Climate Landscape report exceeded the reader's 19 MB limit; only the publisher summary page was reviewed, so claims lack local disaggregation and detailed methods.
The IFRC 2025 mid-year download was rejected as application/octet-stream and GCF SAP048 returned 403; no findings from their search excerpts were used.
Savanes insecurity and seasonal weather stress are both documented but not attributed to one another. Historical 2024 IED-related access restrictions are not current October route conditions.
UNICEF climate-landscape claims use its direct national publisher summary, not inaccessible full-report results.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
